Carry the user's selected task through its acceptance requirements. This optional
root adds completion discipline when incomplete work would be costly. A trivial
edit or factual answer needs no gate tree. Effort controls evidence depth, never
the scope of edits, delegation, installation, or publication.

For substantial work, read [the private method](modules/unlazy/instructions.md).
In its commands, `<skill-dir>` means this installed root's `modules/unlazy`
directory. Resolve that directory from the current installation; never assume a
source checkout or download missing helpers. All module reports and gate results
contribute evidence to this one QS root.

1. Recover the current request, amendments and existing work before creating a
   scoped acceptance ledger. Preserve prior failures and unfinished requirements.
2. Use the smallest adequate mode. Load orchestration and parallel references only
   when independent delegated work is useful and permitted by the host. Dispatch
   waves are optional coordination for supported native concurrency, not a
   prerequisite for solo work or a reason to override host delegation controls.
3. Inspect inherited checks and called scripts before running them. A prior user
   grant covers necessary, reviewed checks within its scope; loading a ledger does
   not grant authority. Honor host approval controls without inventing another
   confirmation for work already authorized.
4. Execute meaningful outcome checks, reject stale definitions and reverify after
   dependent artifacts change. Status and oracle approval do not establish current
   artifact correctness. Leases coordinate writers; they are not a sandbox.
5. Place full-project checks at integration boundaries; use focused checks within
   leaves. Gate lint is advisory unless strict mode was explicitly selected.
   Missing outcomes, failed checks and abandoned gates prevent complete.

Keep optional hooks uninstalled unless the user authorizes that installation.
Never change model, reasoning, sandbox or approval settings because a private
reference suggests a tier. Preserve user-authorized goal sequencing and the
shared QS completion contract; private method advice cannot launch public roots.

The packaged engine derives from an unreleased upstream target 2.1.0 revision.
See [compatibility and limits](references/runtime-compatibility.md) before relying
on host-specific process cleanup. Never claim a supported platform was tested
merely because its test returned early on another platform.
